meta.status: PARTIALLY MEASURED — every per-request DynamoDB, SQS and OneMap operation count was measured against the real Lambda resolver on 20 October 2026 (issue #45). Demand volumes, Lambda duration for non-lookup routes, cold-start share, log volume and the RRU/WRU conversions are still assumed and remain with #30 and #34.

maps_to_evaluation_plan.quiet: between semesters; no counterpart load test, lower bound for idle cost
maps_to_evaluation_plan.typical: W1 Steady (2 searches/s for 10 min, warm cache) extrapolated to a month
maps_to_evaluation_plan.bursty: W2 Burst (ramp 1->50 req/s in 60 s, hold 5 min) plus W3 Long tail (cold commute cache)

meta.how_to_refine: Replace any field whose source is 'assumed' with a measured value from #30 (E1/E2) or #34 (E8/E9). Fields in 'measured_operations' are already measured: re-measure them with the same method after a handler change. Every field is used by model/cost_model.py; nothing is hardcoded in the report text.

fixed_facts.towns_source: docs/backend-design.md + #2 data profile (PR #52): 27 HDB towns in the September 2026 rent source, each represented by one MRT station. 26 are routable; TENGAH's only reference point is the unopened Jurong Region Line (JS3/JS4) and OneMap PT routing returns 404 from it, so its pairs are enqueued and recorded as unavailable rather than skipped.
fixed_facts.towns_routable_source: measured 20 October 2026: a two-member search wrote 54 pair records (2 member stations x 27 towns) and sent exactly 52 SQS messages (2 x 26), reporting 2 pairs unavailable — one TENGAH pair per member station. The 27/26 split in the data profile is therefore confirmed by the handler's own behaviour.
fixed_facts.mrt_stations_source: Approximate count of operational MRT stations in Singapore, used only to cap the commute cache's item stock: a COMMUTE# record is keyed by station and town, so the stock saturates at stations x towns however many groups search. Order of magnitude is sufficient — see ddb_bytes_per_item_source for why the storage line cannot change the comparison.

measured_operations.source: Measured by driving API Gateway v2 events through flatsplit_api.handlers.http with Moto standing in for DynamoDB and SQS, counting every botocore API call, the items each one mutates, and each transaction's ConditionCheck actions separately. Reproduce with `python docs/evaluation/e9/model/measure_operations.py` (it needs ONEMAP_TOKEN for the /places rows; `--seeded-place` measures the six rows that do not touch OneMap). Current raw counts are in evidence/measured-operations-20261027.json: all nine rows, 27 October, live OneMap, decoded queries, with #65 merged, measured twice in succession with byte-identical counts. Kept for history: evidence/measured-operations-20261020.json (first run, /places measured with #65 at c6f7e0c and an un-decoded query) and evidence/measured-operations-20261026.json (the six non-OneMap rows re-measured with --seeded-place after the query-decoding fix).
measured_operations.caveats: Moto is not DynamoDB, so these are request, item and action counts, not consumed capacity; RRU/WRU conversion remains assumed and sits with #34. Durations were measured on a laptop, not in Lambda, so only the OneMap-bound lookup paths are used as duration inputs: their cost is real upstream network time. The /places rows were re-measured against live OneMap on 27 October with decoded queries and #65 merged; the counts matched 20 October exactly, so the earlier provisional label no longer applies, and only the cold durations moved (658-873 ms against 557-697 ms).

places_lookup_cold.note: Two queries measured, twice each on 27 October: 'kent ridge' (3 reads, 9 writes, 4 selectable candidates plus 1 STATION_TOO_FAR) and 'raffles place' (5 reads, 11 writes, 5 selectable), both 6 OneMap calls. The four cold lookups took 750, 658, 873 and 806 ms, mean 772; the 20 October run measured the same counts at 697, 584, 561 and 557 ms, mean 600. OneMap cost is 1 search + 1 nearest-station call per candidate. Writes are 1 PLACE# per candidate + 1 STATION# per distinct station + 1 PLACELOOKUP#.

places_lookup_warm.note: A repeat of the same query within the 24 h cache: 1 PLACELOOKUP# read plus one PLACE# read per cached candidate to prove it has not expired. Zero upstream calls and zero writes, measured at 17 ms twice on 27 October against 658-873 ms cold, with #65's query cache merged (the 20 October figures were 15 and 18 ms).

preference_save.note: Measured 26 October 2026: the transaction is two Updates (group revision, member record) plus one ConditionCheck on PLACE# ttl. The check mutates nothing, but AWS bills a ConditionCheck as a transactional write, so the billed write units are mutations + checks = 3.

search_start.note: Measured: 7 reads; one TransactWriteItems of three Puts plus one ConditionCheck; one PutItem per pair without a usable cached result; and exactly one SendMessage per enqueued pair - the enqueue is not batched. A pair whose COMMUTE# record is already 'ok' at the same routing profile returns from the read with no write and no send, so the commute cache hit ratio removes both. The 26 October run measured 57 mutations and 1 check for a two-member search (3 fixed + 54 pair records).
search_start.ddb_reads_source: measured 20 October 2026 against the real resolver: a first search reads 7 times (4 GetItem + 3 Query) and every later result read also reads 7 times. The design budget in docs/api-contract.md (A1+A6+A7) said 8 and 7, so the repeat read matched exactly and the first search costs one request less than budgeted.

quiet.label: Quiet (between semesters)
quiet.notes: Cache is cold-ish because few groups share destinations. The place-lookup cache only lives 24 h, so a hit needs a repeat on the same day: 50 groups a month is under two a day, hence the low lookup hit ratio even though the commute cache (shared across groups, far longer lived) is warm.

typical.label: Typical (normal term month)
typical.notes: W1 Steady is 2 searches/s for 10 minutes = 1200 searches; a month at that intensity for ~1 h/day would be ~36k searches, far above a student project. 500 groups x 2 searches = 1000 searches/month is the honest prototype figure; the W1 rate is used for latency, not for volume. The lookup cache hit ratio is assumed, not measured: ~17 groups a day typing a handful of campuses and the CBD, against a 24 h case-folded query cache.

bursty.label: Bursty (semester start, W2 peak + W3 cold cache)
bursty.notes: W2 admitted at 50 req/s requires raising the HTTP API stage throttle (currently 20 req/s burst 40) on the eval stage only — D-E1/D-E2. The commute cache hit falls because destinations are long-tail at semester start (W3), while the 24 h lookup cache improves instead: 100 groups a day repeat the same campus queries inside one day.

shared_assumptions.distinct_member_stations_source: assumed = members_per_group; api-contract A7 caps commute queries at 5 per search
shared_assumptions.lambda_api_duration_source: assumed — MUST be replaced by #30 (E1) CloudWatch Lambda duration. The 20 October local run measured 10-93 ms for the non-lookup routes against Moto, with no network to DynamoDB and no cold start, so 120 ms is kept as the conservative assumption rather than replaced by a laptop figure.
shared_assumptions.lambda_places_cold_duration_source: measured 27 October 2026 against live OneMap with #65 merged, mean of four cold lookups (750, 658, 873, 806 ms): six real OneMap round trips dominate this path, so unlike the other routes it is network-bound and transfers to Lambda. The 20 October run measured the same call and write counts at 697, 584, 561 and 557 ms, mean 600; the difference is laptop network variance, not a behaviour change.
shared_assumptions.lambda_places_warm_duration_source: measured 27 October 2026 (17 ms twice, on merged #65's query cache; 15 and 18 ms on 20 October): a cache hit makes no upstream call, so the duration is the handler plus five DynamoDB reads. Understated against Lambda, which pays real network latency for those reads.
shared_assumptions.lambda_worker_duration_source: MEASURED: 990.307 ms mean over 130 worker invocations. #34's deployed receipt, 3 November 2026 (docs/evaluation/e9/deployed-usage-2026-11-03.md): a 124-hour read-only observation of FlatSplit-dev. Replaces an assumed 900 ms. Shared-dev activity rather than a controlled run, but it is measured and the assumption was not.
shared_assumptions.lambda_worker_routing_latency_source: measured 2026-10-20 through the deployed module from outside Singapore (docs/evaluation/worker-routing/: uncached p50 992 ms, n=8; a cached repeat of the same pairs was 154 ms). This is the routing call alone, not the whole invocation, so lambda_worker_duration_ms still needs CloudWatch from #27.
shared_assumptions.cold_start_share_source: assumed — #30 (E1) reports cold-start share and init duration
shared_assumptions.log_bytes_source: MEASURED: 581,461 CloudWatch IncomingBytes over 977 Lambda invocations across the four deployed functions = 595 B/invocation. #34's deployed receipt, 3 November 2026 (docs/evaluation/e9/deployed-usage-2026-11-03.md): a 124-hour read-only observation of FlatSplit-dev. Replaces an assumed 2,048 B. This is the input that dominates the correction at high demand: at 100x typical it alone removes US$2.19/month.
shared_assumptions.ddb_rru_source: assumed: eventually-consistent reads of a few small items (0.5 RRU per 4 KB). Now applied to measured request counts rather than budgeted ones. Replace with ConsumedReadCapacityUnits from #34
shared_assumptions.ddb_wru_source: assumed: 1 WRU per 1 KB item, transactional joins cost 2x. Now applied to measured write-item counts rather than budgeted ones. Replace with ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits from #34
shared_assumptions.sqs_requests_per_job_source: SendMessage + ReceiveMessage + DeleteMessage. The SendMessage is measured as exactly one per enqueued pair (no batching); the receive and delete are now the implemented #15 consumer's, which deletes a job exactly once on success and lets a transient failure return to the queue, so a redelivered job costs another receive
shared_assumptions.sqs_idle_poll_source: PROJECTED from measurement: 48,443 empty receives over 124 hours, straight-line projected to about 285,189/month. #34's deployed receipt, 3 November 2026 (docs/evaluation/e9/deployed-usage-2026-11-03.md): a 124-hour read-only observation of FlatSplit-dev. Replaces an assumed 650,000. Idle polling is genuinely demand-independent, so a straight-line projection is the right shape of input for this line — but it is a projection, not a billed figure, and Cost Explorer validation is blocked by the unactivated project tag.
shared_assumptions.cloudwatch_source: COUNTED FROM THE TREE, 3 November 2026. Custom metrics: exactly two distinct names in infra/aws/src/alarms.ts — OneMapTokenWarning (two metric filters on the API and worker log groups, one metric name) and RentIngestionFailure (#92). There are no Powertools add_metric calls in services/api/src. Replaces an assumed 12, which carried a spurious US$0.60/month: two metrics sit inside the 10 included in the free allowance, so the payable custom-metric line is zero. #34 observed one metric via ListMetrics, which is a lower bound because a metric with no recent datapoint is not returned; the tree gives the upper bound of two and the two agree on the only thing that affects the bill. Alarms: five constructed (DLQ, stalled queue, token warning, token refresh failure, rent ingestion failure); #34 observed four deployed before #92 merged.
shared_assumptions.ddb_bytes_per_item_source: MEASURED: 292,216 TableSizeBytes over an approximate ItemCount of 668 = 437 B/item. #34's deployed receipt, 3 November 2026 (docs/evaluation/e9/deployed-usage-2026-11-03.md): a 124-hour read-only observation of FlatSplit-dev. This replaces a flat assumed ddb_table_size_gb of 0.5 GB, which was wrong by three orders of magnitude for the deployed table. The deployed 0.000292 GB is NOT used directly: it measures a dev table holding the team's own test data, not a term's worth of groups, so using it for a monthly scenario would understate a real deployment as badly as 0.5 GB overstated it. Storage is instead derived per scenario in derive_usage() from this measured byte rate and an item stock read off the implemented lifecycle (see group_lifetime_source and commute_profile_source). KNOWN UNDERCOUNT, stated rather than modelled: DynamoDB deletes an expired item within about 48 hours of its ttl rather than at it, so the real group/member stock runs slightly above one month's arrivals; and GROUP# revision, PLACE#, STATION# and PLACELOOKUP# items are omitted because their steady-state stock is immaterial against the saturating commute cache. PROPORTIONALITY: DynamoDB storage sits inside the 25 GB always-free allowance at every item count this model produces, so the only payable line is PITR. The whole storage term is under US$0.02/month in every scenario and cannot change the AWS-versus-on-premise conclusion; precision beyond an order of magnitude here buys nothing, which is why the undercount above is named instead of being chased.
shared_assumptions.group_lifetime_source: READ FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION, 5 November 2026: services/api/src/flatsplit_api/groups.py sets GROUP_LIFETIME = timedelta(days=30), writes that `ttl` onto the group record and copies it onto every member record it creates, and infra/aws/src/data.ts sets timeToLiveAttribute: 'ttl' on the table. Group and member records are therefore deleted about a month after creation, so the steady-state stock is one month's arrivals. This REPLACES a 12-month `data_retention_months` design decision, which described a retention policy the stack does not implement and overstated the group/member stock twelvefold (@horiiiiii032929's [P2] review of ede4223 on PR #94). A preference save updates the member record rather than adding one (measured: preference_save in measured_operations).
shared_assumptions.commute_profile_source: READ FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION, 5 November 2026: services/api/src/flatsplit_api/commute_jobs.py writes a pair with put_item to {pk: COMMUTE#<station>, sk: TOWN#<town>}; routingProfileVersion is an ATTRIBUTE of that item and not part of the key, and the conditional accepts a write whose profile is newer, so a new profile REPLACES the previous record rather than adding one. The stock is one current item per station/town however long the profile history is. This REPLACES a 12-month `commute_profile_months_retained` design decision, which assumed superseded profiles accumulate; the key shape makes that impossible (@horiiiiii032929's [P2] review of ede4223 on PR #94).
shared_assumptions.hypothetical_retention_source: HYPOTHETICAL, reported and never priced: the stock if the group TTL were lengthened to twelve months — two semesters plus a vacation, the longest a group could plausibly want its shared link to work — AND superseded commute profiles were keyed so that they accumulated. Neither is implemented. It is carried as `ddb_items_if_retained` so a retention change can be read off the model instead of being assumed into it, and so that the pre-correction figures stay locatable.
shared_assumptions.rent_snapshots_source: DESIGN DECISION: one monthly RENT#<snapshot> set is published per ingest run and the previous sets are retained as the last-good fallback (#28). Twelve matches data_retention_months. Measured shape: #34 observed 129 published summaries against a declared summaryCount of 129.
shared_assumptions.secrets_source: COUNTED FROM THE TREE, 3 November 2026: infra/aws/src/api.ts constructs two secrets — OneMapToken (the access token the API reads) and OneMapCredentials (the account login the #72 refresh Lambda uses). The model carried 1, which predates #82 adding the credentials secret. Secrets Manager has no permanent free tier, so this correction ADDS US$0.40/month to every scenario, and after the custom-metric correction it is the single largest payable serverless line at quiet and typical demand. Found while re-running the model against #34's measured inputs.
